title: Unconditional Certified Randomness without Structure
abstract: We obtain a certified randomness protocol in the quantum random oracle model. The protocol is non-interactive and publicly verifiable with a classical verifier, and is based on Yamakawa and Zhandry's proof of quantumness [JACM'24]. We prove unconditional security of this protocol against adversaries making subexponentially-many adaptive quantum queries to the random oracle. Prior work on certified randomness relative to a random oracle additionally assumed the Aaronson--Ambainis conjecture or proved security only against low query-depth adversaries.

bite.hook: We achieve unconditional certified randomness in the quantum random oracle model against subexponential queries.
tldr: Developed a certified randomness protocol in the quantum random oracle model.
Used a non-interactive and publicly verifiable design based on a specific proof of quantumness.
Proved unconditional security against adversaries making adaptive quantum queries.
bite.whyItMatters: Provably secure random numbers are vital for cryptography, and removing unproven assumptions makes digital security much more reliable.
bite.eli5: Imagine flipping a coin where a brilliant mathematician can mathematically prove the flip was truly fair and unpredictable, without needing to trust any special rules.
